name: 5-Minute Miso Glazed Salmon
headnote: J. Kenji Lopez-Alt presents this as one of the handful of reliable dishes worth knowing by heart - fast, nearly cleanup-free, and doable in a toaster oven without smelling up the apartment. The marinade of miso, sake, sugar, soy sauce and oil is really a surface treatment doing several jobs at once: the salty miso and soy act as a brine that helps the flesh hold moisture and add glutamates for savoriness, while the thick miso paste insulates the fillet so it heats gently and evenly. Sugar caramelizes to speed up charring and the oil transfers heat so the surface sizzles evenly, which is why thick fillets of at least an inch matter - the outside chars while the center stays rare to medium-rare at roughly 115 to 125 F. He also advises watching the broiler's on-off cycle and wedging the door slightly open to keep the element firing, and folding the foil up as a shield over any spot browning too fast.
comment_digest: The most concrete failure mode reported is a weak broiler: one cook's toaster oven baked the fish rather than charring it and plans to use the gas oven broiler instead, while another with a thick fillet found the timing off, reverted to 425 F convection and finished under the broiler with only fair results, also feeling the marinade did not penetrate much. That echoes the article's own warning about broiler cycling. Suggested additions include a small amount of chili oil, up to a tablespoon, and sriracha mayo alongside. The excess marinade is not wasted - one reviewer drizzled it over kale, fennel and shallot roasting in the same toaster oven, started seven minutes earlier. Two questions go to the page rather than the cook: what the green garnish in the photo is, since it is not in the ingredients, and what to do with the rest of the sake bottle.
flags: Comment section is thin on technique corrections and several entries are one-word praise. The photographed green garnish is not listed in the ingredients or directions, which one reader queries. Some comments end in 'Read More' and may be truncated; two threads show 'View Replies' whose contents are not in the paste.
